claims.statement: The European Commission's Cloud Sovereignty Framework (v1.2.1, October 2025) defines eight sovereignty objectives (SOV-1 to SOV-8), each assessed on a Sovereignty Effective Assurance Level from SEAL-0 to SEAL-4; contracting authorities set a minimum SEAL per objective and rank bids on a weighted score. The Commission used it in its 2026 cloud procurement.

source.title: European Commission: cloud sovereignty through strategic procurement (17 Apr 2026)

claims.notes: Weights per most secondary sources: SOV-1 15%, SOV-2 10%, SOV-3 10%, SOV-4 15%, SOV-5 20%, SOV-6 15%, SOV-7 10%, SOV-8 5% (one source differs). SEAL-3 label ("digital resilience" vs "technological autonomy") not settled; confirm against the Commission PDF. claims.statement: France, Law no. 2024-449 (SREN) Art. 31: State administrations, certain State operators and listed public interest groupings that use cloud services for data of particular sensitivity (data covered by secrets protected by law, or needed for essential State missions) must use services meeting protection criteria tied to ANSSI SecNumCloud or an equivalent European certification. The implementing decree listing the groupings was reported published on 16 April 2026.

source.title: TRIS notification of the SREN Art. 31 implementing decree (European Commission)

claims.statement: French operators of vital importance (OIV) are required to use SecNumCloud-qualified services for sensitive data.
claims.basisNote: No source found in S2. Settle: Code de la défense (OIV provisions), ANSSI guidance or sector orders on Légifrance. Until then the FR_SECNUMCLOUD rule for critical-infrastructure operators is consultant-only.

claims.statement: Germany, SGB V § 393: healthcare providers under Chapter 4 SGB V, statutory health and long-term care insurers and their processors may process health and social data in cloud services only with a current BSI C5 attestation for the cloud systems used (with the customer criteria implemented); a C5 Type 1 attestation counted as current until 30 June 2025, a Type 2 attestation is required from 1 July 2025.
claims.notes: Commentary notes it is unclear whether the attestation duty falls on the provider, its processor or both.
